methodology: There is no single authoritative public list of the '100 most widely spoken languages': published rankings differ in how they count second-language (L2) speakers, how they split or merge macrolanguages and varieties (e.g. Arabic, Chinese, Persian, Serbo-Croatian, Hindi and related languages), and in the census data they rely on. The entries tagged 'top-100-seed' were compiled from widely published total-speaker (L1+L2) rankings, such as the summaries Ethnologue publishes, and are a seed list only. TODO: this seed list has NOT yet been reconciled against a single cited, dated dataset; until it is, the tag means 'appears in commonly published top-100 rankings', not 'verified rank'. No speaker counts are recorded here. Further entries were added so that (a) every UN member state has at least one entry for a language it designates as official or uses as its national/administrative language ('national-official'; 'un-official' marks the six official languages of the United Nations), (b) Modern Standard Arabic and major spoken Arabic varieties are represented ('variety', with variantOf pointing to the standard), and (c) a selection of regional and Indigenous languages from every inhabited continent is included ('regional-indigenous'). Inclusion in this registry says nothing about translation availability: see translationStatus and reviewStatus. Tags follow BCP 47 as used by Unicode CLDR; see docs/i18n/language-registry.md.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Canonical source language for Lumenary content. All current English content is AI-drafted and has not been reviewed by a named human, so reviewStatus is 'unreviewed' even though translationStatus is 'canonical'.

languages.name: Chinese (Simplified)
languages.notes: Demo UI locale: interface strings and any content in this language are machine drafts and have not been reviewed by a human. Standard Chinese (the Mandarin-based written and spoken standard, Putonghua) in Simplified characters. Speaker rankings count Mandarin (ISO 639-3 cmn); CLDR uses the macrolanguage code 'zh' with script subtags. Other Sinitic languages (yue, wuu, nan, hak) are separate entries.

languages.name: Chinese (Traditional)
languages.notes: Standard written Chinese in Traditional characters. Listed separately from zh-Hans because the scripts are not interchangeable for learners; CLDR does not make zh-Hant inherit from zh-Hans. Terminology and conventions differ between Taiwan and Hong Kong/Macau (CLDR has zh-Hant-TW and zh-Hant-HK), so a translation must declare which it follows. Included for Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau; Mandarin speakers are counted under zh-Hans in speaker rankings, so this entry is not tagged top-100-seed.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.notes: Demo UI locale: interface strings and any content in this language are machine drafts and have not been reviewed by a human. Standard Hindi in Devanagari. Indian census figures for Hindi include several related languages (e.g. Bhojpuri, Awadhi, Magahi, Chhattisgarhi) that are listed separately here. Fiji Hindi is a separate entry (hif).

languages.name: Spanish
languages.notes: Demo UI locale: interface strings and any content in this language are machine drafts and have not been reviewed by a human. One registry entry for all Spanish. CLDR provides es-419 (Latin America and the Caribbean) and country locales (es-MX, es-AR, ...); regional mathematical vocabulary differences are recorded in the glossary rather than as separate translations. A region subtag must not be used unless content was genuinely adapted for that region.

languages.name: Arabic (Modern Standard)
languages.notes: Demo UI locale: interface strings and any content in this language are machine drafts and have not been reviewed by a human. Modern Standard Arabic (ISO 639-3 arb; CLDR uses the macrolanguage code 'ar'). It is the written standard for schooling across the Arabic-speaking world, but nobody's everyday spoken variety. Spoken varieties are separate entries with variantOf 'ar'. Mathematical notation direction and digit shapes vary by country; see docs/i18n/language-registry.md.

languages.name: French
languages.notes: In several countries (e.g. Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger) French was recently reclassified by constitution or charter as a working language rather than an official language; see countries.json.

languages.name: Portuguese
languages.notes: Brazilian and European Portuguese differ in some mathematical vocabulary and conventions (CLDR: pt-BR is the default 'pt', pt-PT is separate).

languages.name: Indonesian
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR; commonly called 'Bahasa Indonesia'. Closely related to Malay (ms) but a separate standard.

languages.name: Urdu
languages.notes: Usually typeset in the Nastaliq style of Arabic script, which needs suitable fonts and line-height for mathematics.

languages.name: Japanese
languages.notes: Japan has no statutory official language; Japanese is the de facto national language. Script 'Jpan' = Han + Hiragana + Katakana.

languages.name: Nigerian Pidgin
languages.notes: Native name as given in CLDR; 'Naijá' is also used. No single orthography is universally adopted.

languages.name: Egyptian Arabic
languages.notes: Everyday spoken Arabic of Egypt (ISO 639-3 arz). Schooling uses Modern Standard Arabic; an arz translation would be a genuinely different text, not ar with an EG region subtag. Native name: also 'العامية المصرية' (Egyptian colloquial).

languages.name: Marathi
languages.notes: Official language of Maharashtra; one of the 22 languages of India's Eighth Schedule.

languages.name: Telugu
languages.notes: Official in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Hausa
languages.notes: Also written in Ajami (Arabic script). Designated the national language of Niger by the March 2025 transitional charter.

languages.name: Tamil
languages.notes: Official in Sri Lanka and Singapore and in Tamil Nadu (India).

languages.name: Swahili
languages.notes: Demo UI locale: interface strings and any content in this language are machine drafts and have not been reviewed by a human. Standard Swahili (ISO 639-3 swh; 'sw' is the macrolanguage code used by CLDR). Mathematical vocabulary differs between Tanzania, where primary schooling is in Swahili, and Kenya, where mathematics is generally taught in English; see the glossary. Congo Swahili (swc) is a distinct variety not covered here.

languages.name: Punjabi (Shahmukhi)
languages.notes: Punjabi as written in Pakistan in Shahmukhi (Perso-Arabic) script. CLDR models this as pa-Arab; ISO 639-3 has a separate code pnb (Western Punjabi). Readers of Shahmukhi generally cannot read Gurmukhi, so no variantOf/fallback to 'pa' is set; a fallback to 'ur' needs a deliberate decision.

languages.name: Wu Chinese
languages.notes: Spoken Sinitic language of Shanghai, Zhejiang and southern Jiangsu. Schooling uses Standard Chinese; fallback is zh-Hans.

languages.name: Filipino
languages.notes: National language of the Philippines, based on Tagalog (tl). CLDR uses 'fil'.

languages.name: Korean
languages.notes: Called 조선말 (Chosŏnmal) in the DPRK; standard vocabulary and spelling differ somewhat between the two Koreas.

languages.name: Persian
languages.notes: Iranian Persian (ISO 639-3 pes; 'fa' is the macrolanguage code). Dari (prs) and Tajik (tg) are separate entries. Persian uses its own digit shapes (CLDR numbering system 'arabext').

languages.name: Javanese
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR ('Basa Jawa' is common). Traditionally also written in Javanese script (Java).

languages.name: Gujarati
languages.notes: Official in Gujarat; Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Thai
languages.notes: Thai has its own digits (CLDR numbering system 'thai'), although Western digits are common.

languages.name: Amharic
languages.notes: Federal working language of Ethiopia.

languages.name: Kannada
languages.notes: Official in Karnataka; Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Bhojpuri
languages.notes: Often counted under Hindi in Indian census data. Mathematics schooling for Bhojpuri speakers is normally in Hindi.

languages.name: Cantonese
languages.notes: Main spoken language of Hong Kong and Macau; schooling there uses Standard Written Chinese in Traditional characters, read aloud in Cantonese. CLDR has yue-Hant (default) and yue-Hans (Guangdong). A 'yue' text means written Cantonese, which differs from zh-Hant.

languages.name: Punjabi (Gurmukhi)
languages.notes: Punjabi in Gurmukhi script as used in India (official in Punjab). Shahmukhi Punjabi is pa-Arab.

languages.name: Min Nan Chinese
languages.notes: Includes Hokkien and Taiwanese (台語). Written in Han characters and in Latin romanisations (Pe̍h-ōe-jī, Tâi-lô). Script recorded as Hant because Taiwan's education ministry publishes recommended Traditional characters for it; mainland speakers write Simplified characters. No variantOf is set because the right fallback (zh-Hant or zh-Hans) depends on the learner's region.

languages.name: Yoruba
languages.notes: Tone diacritics and underdots must be preserved; fonts must support them.

languages.name: Burmese
languages.notes: Burmese has its own digits (CLDR numbering system 'mymr').

languages.name: Odia
languages.notes: Official in Odisha; Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Malayalam
languages.notes: Official in Kerala; Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Algerian Arabic
languages.notes: Everyday spoken Arabic of Algeria ('Darja', also 'Dziri'). No widely adopted standard orthography; also written in Latin script informally.

languages.name: Sudanese Arabic
languages.notes: Native name given in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Moroccan Arabic
languages.notes: Everyday spoken Arabic of Morocco ('Darija').

languages.name: Uzbek
languages.notes: Latin script is official in Uzbekistan but Cyrillic remains widely used; in Afghanistan Uzbek is written in Arabic script (CLDR uz-Arab, uz-Cyrl).

languages.name: Sindhi
languages.notes: Official in Sindh (Pakistan); Eighth Schedule language in India, where Devanagari is also used (CLDR sd-Deva).

languages.name: Azerbaijani
languages.notes: Latin script in Azerbaijan; in Iran, Azerbaijani (South Azerbaijani, ISO 639-3 azb) is written in Arabic script (CLDR az-Arab).

languages.name: Kurdish (Kurmanji)
languages.notes: CLDR uses 'ku' for Northern Kurdish (Kurmanji, ISO 639-3 kmr) in Latin script; 'ku' is also the ISO macrolanguage code for all Kurdish. Central Kurdish (Sorani) is ckb.

languages.name: Central Kurdish (Sorani)
languages.notes: Kurdish is an official language of Iraq; in the Kurdistan Region it is mainly Sorani in Arabic script, with Kurmanji (Badini) also used. Native name per CLDR; 'کوردی' or 'سۆرانی' are also common.

languages.name: Oromo
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR; speakers also say 'Afaan Oromoo'. Official language of the Oromia regional state; reported as an additional federal working language of Ethiopia from 2020 (implementation to be verified).

languages.name: Malay
languages.notes: Standard Malay (ISO 639-3 zsm; 'ms' is the macrolanguage code). Native name per CLDR ('Bahasa Melayu' is common). Jawi (Arabic script) is also used, notably in Brunei.

languages.name: Fula
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR ('Pulaar'); the eastern varieties call it 'Fulfulde' and Guinea's 'Pular'. Macrolanguage with substantial regional variation. Also written in Adlam script (CLDR ff-Adlm) and Ajami. A real translation must target a specific variety.

languages.name: Cebuano
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR; 'Cebuano' and 'Sinugbuanong Binisaya' are also used.

languages.name: Assamese
languages.notes: Official in Assam; Eighth Schedule language. Uses the Bengali-Assamese script (ISO 15924 Beng).

languages.name: Maithili
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language in India; widely spoken in Nepal.

languages.name: Kinyarwanda
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR; speakers also write 'Ikinyarwanda'.

languages.name: Kazakh
languages.notes: Kazakhstan has an announced transition to Latin script whose timetable has changed several times; in China Kazakh is written in Arabic script.

languages.name: Akan
languages.notes: Macrolanguage including Twi and Fante, which have distinct written standards.

languages.name: Hiligaynon
languages.notes: Also called Ilonggo.

languages.name: Serbian (Cyrillic)
languages.notes: CLDR default for 'sr' is Cyrillic. Serbian is also widely written in Latin script (sr-Latn, separate entry). Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian and Montenegrin are mutually intelligible standard varieties; speaker rankings sometimes count them together as Serbo-Croatian.

languages.name: Lingala
languages.notes: National language (not official) of the DR Congo and the Republic of the Congo.

languages.name: Chittagonian
languages.notes: No standardised written form; when written, usually in Bengali script. Native name and spelling to be confirmed by a speaker. Schooling for speakers is in Bengali.

languages.name: Uyghur
languages.notes: Written in a fully vowelled Arabic-based alphabet in China; Cyrillic is used by some speakers in Central Asia.

languages.name: Awadhi
languages.notes: Often counted under Hindi in Indian census data.

languages.name: Chichewa (Nyanja)
languages.notes: Called Chichewa in Malawi and Nyanja in Zambia; 'Chewa' is one of Zimbabwe's officially recognised languages.

languages.name: Quechua
languages.notes: Macrolanguage (ISO 639-3 lists dozens of Quechua languages). Southern Quechua is the main variety in Peru and Bolivia; Ecuadorian Kichwa differs. A real translation must target a specific variety and orthography.

languages.name: Bambara
languages.notes: Official language of Mali (one of the national languages made official by the 2023 constitution). Also written in N'Ko script (CLDR bm-Nkoo).

languages.name: Wolof
languages.notes: National language of Senegal; also written in Ajami (Wolofal).

languages.name: Mossi
languages.notes: Most widely spoken language of Burkina Faso.

languages.name: Hebrew
languages.notes: Mathematical expressions are normally typeset left-to-right inside right-to-left Hebrew text.

languages.name: Tajik
languages.notes: A variety of Persian written in Cyrillic; not interchangeable with fa/prs for learners because of the script.

languages.name: Hakka Chinese
languages.notes: Script recorded as Hant because Taiwan (where Hakka is a national language) publishes Traditional-character and romanised standards; mainland speakers write Simplified characters. No variantOf set (fallback depends on region).

languages.name: Sylheti
languages.notes: Usually written in Bengali script; the historical Syloti Nagri script (ISO 15924 Sylo) is also used. Schooling for speakers is in Bengali.

languages.name: Mesopotamian (Iraqi) Arabic
languages.notes: Everyday spoken Arabic of Iraq. Native name given in the commonly attested form.

languages.name: Levantine Arabic
languages.notes: ISO 639-3 change request 2022-006 (effective 2023-01-20) retired the code ajp (South Levantine Arabic), merged it into apc, and renamed apc from 'North Levantine Arabic' to 'Levantine Arabic'. Jordanian and Palestinian Arabic, formerly ajp, are therefore covered by apc. The IANA registry keeps 'ajp' with Preferred-Value 'apc'; normalise any incoming ajp tags to apc.

languages.name: Tunisian Arabic
languages.notes: Everyday spoken Arabic of Tunisia ('Tounsi', 'Derja').

languages.name: Gulf Arabic
languages.notes: Spoken Arabic of the Gulf coast. Native name given in the commonly attested form.

languages.name: Libyan Arabic
languages.notes: Native name given in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Hassaniya Arabic
languages.notes: Spoken Arabic of Mauritania and neighbouring areas; Hassaniya is one of the 13 national languages that Mali's 2023 constitution makes official. Also written in Latin script.

languages.name: Dari
languages.notes: Afghan Persian (ISO 639-3 prs). CLDR models it as fa-AF; 'prs' is used here so that it can be a separate translation target with fallback to 'fa'.

languages.name: Serbian (Latin)
languages.notes: Script variant of 'sr'. CLDR does not make sr-Latn inherit from sr (Cyrillic), so no variantOf is set; transliteration between the two is mechanical but must still be checked.

languages.name: Bosnian
languages.notes: Also written in Cyrillic (CLDR bs-Cyrl).

languages.name: Montenegrin
languages.notes: ISO 639-3 code cnr assigned in 2017. Written in both Latin and Cyrillic. CLDR coverage is minimal at the time of writing (to be checked).

languages.name: Norwegian Bokmål
languages.notes: One of the two written standards of Norwegian ('no' is the macrolanguage code). CLDR uses nb and nn.

languages.name: Norwegian Nynorsk
languages.notes: The second written standard of Norwegian; schools in Nynorsk municipalities teach in it.

languages.name: Irish
languages.notes: First official language of Ireland under Article 8 of the Constitution; recognised in Northern Ireland.

languages.name: Maltese
languages.notes: A Semitic language written in Latin script.

languages.name: Romansh
languages.notes: Swiss national language; official at federal level for communication with Romansh speakers. Rumantsch Grischun is the federal written standard; regional written idioms are used in schools.

languages.name: Catalan
languages.notes: Sole official language of Andorra; co-official in Catalonia, the Balearic Islands and (as Valencian) the Valencian Community in Spain.

languages.name: Latin
languages.notes: Included because Latin is an official language of the Holy See. Historically important for mathematical terminology; no learner-facing translation is planned.

languages.name: Armenian
languages.notes: Eastern Armenian is the standard in Armenia; Western Armenian (diaspora) differs.

languages.name: Mongolian
languages.notes: Written in Cyrillic in Mongolia, which is reintroducing the traditional Mongolian script (ISO 15924 Mong) for some official uses; in Inner Mongolia (China) the traditional vertical script is used (CLDR mn-Mong).

languages.name: Dzongkha
languages.notes: National language of Bhutan. Much school mathematics in Bhutan is taught in English.

languages.name: Dhivehi
languages.notes: Written right-to-left in Thaana script.

languages.name: Māori
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR; commonly 'te reo Māori'. Official language of New Zealand (Māori Language Act 1987; Te Ture mō Te Reo Māori 2016). Macrons must be preserved.

languages.name: New Zealand Sign Language
languages.notes: Official language of New Zealand (NZSL Act 2006). Sign languages have no conventional written form, so the script is recorded as Zxxx (unwritten) and direction is not meaningful. Included for referential integrity; sign-language content needs video and is outside the current text pipeline.

languages.name: South African Sign Language
languages.notes: Twelfth official language of South Africa (constitutional amendment of 2023). Script recorded as Zxxx (unwritten). Included for referential integrity; sign-language content needs video and is outside the current text pipeline.

languages.name: Fijian
languages.notes: Called iTaukei in Fiji's 2013 Constitution. Native name in the commonly attested form.

languages.name: Fiji Hindi
languages.notes: Written in both Latin and Devanagari scripts; Latin is recorded here. Distinct from Standard Hindi (hi), which is also taught in Fiji.

languages.name: Tok Pisin
languages.notes: Most widely used lingua franca of Papua New Guinea.

languages.name: Bislama
languages.notes: National language of Vanuatu and one of its three official languages.

languages.name: Gilbertese
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Marshallese
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Nauruan
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Palauan
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Tuvaluan
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Chamorro
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Cook Islands Māori
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Niuean
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Tsonga
languages.notes: Recognised in Zimbabwe as 'Shangani'.

languages.name: Southern Ndebele
languages.notes: Distinct from Northern Ndebele (nd) of Zimbabwe.

languages.name: Northern Ndebele
languages.notes: Distinct from Southern Ndebele (nr) of South Africa.

languages.name: Standard Moroccan Tamazight
languages.notes: Official language of Morocco since 2011, standardised by IRCAM and written in Tifinagh.

languages.name: Tamazight (Berber languages)
languages.notes: 'ber' is an ISO 639 collective code (Berber languages), used here only to represent Algeria's constitutionally official 'Tamazight', which covers several varieties (e.g. Kabyle kab, Chaoui, Mozabite, Tuareg). It is a placeholder: any real translation must target a specific variety and script (Latin, Tifinagh and Arabic scripts are all used in Algeria).

languages.name: Comorian (Shingazidja)
languages.notes: Stand-in for 'Shikomori' (Comorian), the official national language of the Comoros, which comprises several varieties (Shingazidja zdj, Shindzuani wni, Shimwali wlc, Shimaore swb). There is no single ISO code for Comorian as a whole.

languages.name: Dyula
languages.notes: Major lingua franca of Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. Also written in N'Ko.

languages.name: Susu
languages.notes: Reported to be among the national languages made official by Guinea's 2025 constitution. Native name in the commonly attested form.

languages.name: Maninka
languages.notes: Eastern Maninkakan (ISO 639-3 emk) as spoken in Guinea; reported to be among the national languages made official by Guinea's 2025 constitution. Widely written in N'Ko script (ISO 15924 Nkoo, right-to-left), which a translation may prefer.

languages.name: Papiamento
languages.notes: Spelled 'Papiamento' in Aruba and 'Papiamentu' in Curaçao and Bonaire; the two islands use different orthographies.

languages.name: Guaraní
languages.notes: Co-official with Spanish in Paraguay (Constitution, Art. 140), where most of the population speaks it.

languages.name: Welsh
languages.notes: Official language in Wales (Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011). Many Welsh schools teach mathematics in Welsh.

languages.name: Scottish Gaelic
languages.notes: Recognised as an official language of Scotland by the Gaelic Language (Scotland) Act 2005.

languages.name: Basque
languages.notes: Co-official in the Basque Country and parts of Navarre.

languages.name: Galician
languages.notes: Co-official in Galicia.

languages.name: Occitan
languages.notes: Aranese (an Occitan variety) is co-official in Catalonia.

languages.name: West Frisian
languages.notes: Official in the Dutch province of Fryslân.

languages.name: Northern Sami
languages.notes: Most widely spoken Sami language; official in Sami administrative areas of Norway, Sweden and Finland. Other Sami languages (e.g. Lule, South, Inari, Skolt) have their own codes.

languages.name: Romani
languages.notes: Macrolanguage with many varieties and no single standard orthography; recognised minority language in many European states. Native name in a commonly attested form.

languages.name: Yiddish
languages.notes: Recognised national minority language in Sweden (and in some other countries); written right-to-left in Hebrew script.

languages.name: Tatar
languages.notes: State language of the Republic of Tatarstan (Russian Federation).

languages.name: Bashkir
languages.notes: State language of the Republic of Bashkortostan.

languages.name: Chechen
languages.notes: State language of the Chechen Republic.

languages.name: Sakha (Yakut)
languages.notes: State language of the Sakha Republic.

languages.name: Kabyle
languages.notes: Most widely spoken Tamazight variety in Algeria; mostly written in Latin script.

languages.name: Kikuyu
languages.notes: CLDR gives 'Gikuyu' without diacritics; the standard orthography 'Gĩkũyũ' is used here deliberately.

languages.name: Luganda
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR; also 'Oluganda'. Most widely spoken language of Uganda.

languages.name: Kongo
languages.notes: Note: the 'Kikongo' that is a national language of the DR Congo and (as Munukutuba) of the Republic of the Congo is usually Kituba (ISO 639-3 ktu), a Kongo-based lingua franca distinct from Kongo proper (kg).

languages.name: Luba-Lulua
languages.notes: National language of the DR Congo.

languages.name: Krio
languages.notes: Lingua franca of Sierra Leone.

languages.name: Dinka
languages.notes: Macrolanguage; native name in the commonly attested form, to be confirmed by a speaker.

languages.name: Kanuri
languages.notes: Macrolanguage. Among the 'spoken languages' recognised by Niger's 2025 charter.

languages.name: Bemba
languages.notes: One of Zambia's seven regional official languages used in early schooling.

languages.name: Mauritian Creole
languages.notes: Most widely spoken home language in Mauritius.

languages.name: Kabuverdianu
languages.notes: Cape Verdean Creole; the constitution of Cabo Verde provides for promoting its eventual official status.

languages.name: Zhuang
languages.notes: Macrolanguage; official Latin orthography in China; traditionally also written in Sawndip (Han-derived characters).

languages.name: Hmong
languages.notes: Macrolanguage; the Romanized Popular Alphabet is common; Pahawh Hmong and Nyiakeng Puachue Hmong scripts also exist.

languages.name: Ainu
languages.notes: Indigenous language of Hokkaido; critically endangered. Recognised by Japan's 2019 Ainu Promotion Act. Written in Katakana (with special small kana) and in Latin script.

languages.name: Sanskrit
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language of India; included because a large body of historical mathematics is written in Sanskrit. Historical attributions must follow reliable scholarship.

languages.name: Konkani
languages.notes: Official in Goa; Eighth Schedule language. Also written in Latin and Kannada scripts.

languages.name: Dogri
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Bodo
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language.

languages.name: Manipuri (Meitei)
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language. Written in Bengali script and increasingly in Meetei Mayek (ISO 15924 Mtei), which Manipur has promoted officially; the script for any translation needs a deliberate choice.

languages.name: Kashmiri
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language; also written in Devanagari (CLDR ks-Deva).

languages.name: Santali
languages.notes: Eighth Schedule language, written in Ol Chiki script (also in Latin, Bengali, Devanagari and Odia scripts).

languages.name: Balochi
languages.notes: Macrolanguage.

languages.name: Nahuatl
languages.notes: 'nah' is an ISO 639 collective code; ISO 639-3 splits Nahuatl into many individual languages (e.g. nhe Eastern Huasteca, nhw Western Huasteca, nch Central Huasteca). A real translation must target a specific variety and orthography. Recognised as a national language of Mexico (General Law of Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples, 2003). Native name in one commonly attested form.

languages.name: Yucatec Maya
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form; spellings vary.

languages.name: Kʼicheʼ
languages.notes: One of the Mayan languages recognised by Guatemala's National Languages Law (2003).

languages.name: Mapudungun
languages.notes: Several competing orthographies exist (also spelled Mapuzugun).

languages.name: Cherokee
languages.notes: Native name per CLDR (Tsalagi); the full phrase ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ is also used. Written in the Cherokee syllabary.

languages.name: Inuktitut
languages.notes: Official in Nunavut and the Northwest Territories; written in Canadian Aboriginal syllabics and in Latin script (Inuinnaqtun). Macrolanguage.

languages.name: Hawaiian
languages.notes: Official language of the State of Hawaii alongside English; Hawaiian-medium schools exist.

languages.name: Sranan Tongo
languages.notes: Lingua franca of Suriname.

languages.name: Jamaican Creole
languages.notes: Widely spoken in Jamaica; schooling is in English. Orthography not standardised in everyday use.

languages.name: Tahitian
languages.notes: Native name in the commonly attested form.

languages.name: Pijin
languages.notes: Lingua franca of Solomon Islands.

languages.name: Warlpiri
languages.notes: One of many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages of Australia; bilingual schooling has existed in some Warlpiri communities.

languages.name: Kriol
languages.notes: English-based creole spoken across northern Australia.
